walkthroughs.body_html:
Forces, Energy & Electricity — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Forces, Energy & Electricity brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Forces, Energy & Electricity.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A motor lifts a 50 kg load 4.0 m in 10 s. What is its useful output power? (g = 9.81 m s⁻²)
Which equation correctly expresses work done?
options: W = mgh
W = Fs cos θ
W = ½mv²
W = Fv

mcqs.q: When energy is 'lost' as heat due to friction, what has really happened?
options: Energy has been transferred to the thermal store of the surroundings — it's not destroyed, just dissipated.
Energy has been converted into mass following E=mc^2.
Energy has been used up and no longer exists.
Kinetic energy stays the same because mass hasn't changed.

mcqs.q: If a car doubles its speed, what happens to its kinetic energy?
options: Kinetic energy stays the same because mass hasn't changed.
Energy has been converted into mass following E=mc^2.
It quadruples (because KE = 1/2 mv^2 — kinetic energy is proportional to v^2).
Kinetic energy doubles because energy is proportional to speed.

mcqs.q: Is the internal energy of a system the same as the heat it contains?
options: Kinetic energy stays the same because mass hasn't changed.
No — a system doesn't 'contain heat'; internal energy is the total kinetic and potential energy of its particles, changed by heating or doing work.
Yes — internal energy is just the stored heat in the object.
No — internal energy refers only to the chemical potential energy.
